messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] runtime-serving: p95 latency spike detected on canary after rollout (p95 ~1.8s, baseline 420ms). Trigger: rollout-1860123400. Link: https://grafana/redwood/runtime/canary (auto)

alex: ack, I'm oncall. grabbing graphs now. canary traffic ~10%?

maria: confirmed. canary nodes show sharp increase in kernel-fallback counts and batching queue depth immediately post-deploy. commit=0xabc123. feature_flag=batching_v2 enabled in canary.

simon: observed KV cache miss rate up x3 on canary. batching latency per-batch jumps -> worker queuing. suspect new batching path triggers kernel fallback for short sequences. snippet from node logs: ```
2026-03-15T18:05:12Z WARN kernel_fallback: kernel_select failed fallback_count=48 seq_len=32 model=redwood-llama-v2
2026-03-15T18:05:12Z INFO batcher: queue_size=72 pending=18
```

alex: could we flip the kill-switch for batching_v2 in canary? if that reduces tail we can decide rollback.

maria: doing: `FLAGCTL set batching_v2 false --env=canary --actor=maria`

deploy-bot: FLAGCTL: batching_v2 -> false (canary) succeeded. ID=flagop-9876

chen: watching metrics. p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 610ms in the last 60s after flag flip. still above baseline but improving.

lisa: CS note: Customer ACME reported slow streaming replies at 18:06 UTC (no 5xxs). I've opened ticket INC-ACME-452 and pinged account execs.

simon: kernel-fallback rate now halved but still elevated. also seeing backlog drain but some worker pods still hitting fallback due to kernel selector heuristic in commit 0xabc123.

alex: next step: pause rollout and rollback canary to stable. initiating: `deploy rollback --service runtime-serving --to-tag stable-2026-03-12 --scope=canary`

deploy-bot: Rollback started for runtime-serving (canary) -> stable-2026-03-12. job=rb-3344

maria: also opening hotfix PR to guard kernel path with a sequence-length check and revert the batching path change until we validate quantization/short-seq behavior.

chen: rollback completed. traffic confirmed shifted back to stable. p95 baseline returning: 430ms -> 460ms in last minute. kernel-fallback counts trending down to normal.

alex: good. customers impacted: ACME (noted), plus transient Latency for small number of premium tenants. no downstream 5xxs or data loss.

lisa: sent ACME update: "We found a regression in a canary rollout that increased tail latency. We rolled back and applied kill-switch; your service should be back to normal. Investigating root cause and follow-up fix."

simon: root cause summary: commit 0xabc123 introduced batching code that triggers a kernel selection fallback for short-sequence requests causing batching backlog and increased KV misses. reproducible locally with short sequences + quantized weights.

maria: follow-up action items: 1) revert commit from rollout, 2) add unit tests for kernel selection paths, 3) gate batching_v2 behind stricter canary checks and integration tests, 4) postmortem doc. I'll file tickets.

ach: (typo note)

achen: (handing off) I'm staying on monitoring until 19:00 UTC then hand to next oncall. all good to close after 30m stable metrics.

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: kernel_fallback/batching_v2 regression. mitigation: feature_flag flip + canary rollback. monitoring continues.

alex: thanks everyone. closing thread; keep an eye and we'll sync in postmortem. :thumbsup:
